project: Crop Health AI — Urban Heat Island & Thermal Downscaling (Visakhapatnam)

aoi_metadata.name: Visakhapatnam
aoi_metadata.urban_typology: Coastal Industrial Port City with Forested Hill Ridges

sensor_specifications.high_res_optical_sensor: Sentinel-2 MSI Level-2A (B2, B3, B4, B8, B11)

downscaling_evaluation_spatial_split.methodology: Yao et al. (2020) Random Forest Thermal Downscaling with Energy-Conserving Residual Preservation
downscaling_evaluation_spatial_split.spatial_split_protocol: Spatial block partitioning (1.92 km x 1.92 km blocks, 11 train blocks, 5 held-out blocks; water excluded)
downscaling_evaluation_spatial_split.scientific_interpretation: On held-out spatial blocks (1.92 km x 1.92 km blocks, 30% spatial split), Random Forest downscaling achieves R² = 0.0608, RMSE = 2.194 °C, and MAE = 1.693 °C on the primary winter scene. Plain Physical Assessment: The modest R² under strict spatial cross-validation is an expected physical consequence of complex coastal-urban terrain. While 2D optical indices capture macro vegetation cooling and built-up warmth, they do not resolve: (1) 3D urban canopy geometry and building shade dynamics, (2) Thermal inertia variations across diverse building materials (concrete vs steel vs roof sheets), (3) Strong maritime sea-breeze microclimate advection along the Bay of Bengal coastline, and (4) Point-source anthropogenic heat plumes from the industrial port and steel processing corridor. The low absolute RMSE confirms that downscaled temperatures remain physically consistent across the municipal domain.

multidate_seasonal_downscaling_evaluatio.seasonal_findings: Pre-monsoon spring (April) exhibits the highest absolute LST (mean 38.59 °C), while mid-winter (December) exhibits the lowest (mean 27.76 °C). Gradient boosting with topographic and coastal predictors improves spatial generalization across complex ridgelines.

diurnal_analysis.description: Day (10:30 AM overpass) vs Night (10:00 PM overpass) thermal contrast
diurnal_analysis.microclimate_insight: High diurnal amplitude (>14 °C) marks unshaded industrial slag and steel storage yards; low diurnal amplitude (<6 °C) marks the maritime coastal interface and dense Simhachalam canopy.

seasonal_analysis.description: Pre-monsoon Summer (April/May) vs Winter (Dec/Jan) thermal contrast

tree_planting_priority_program.program_name: Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) Urban Forest Action Plan
tree_planting_priority_program.estimated_citywide_cooling_benefit: Average -5.3 °C cooling deficit vs canopy reference (upper bound, not a measured effect) across 12 priority parcels (data-derived; species are literature-based suggestions, not computed)

properties.site_name: Site #1: Gajuwaka Industrial Buffer & Slag Corridor
properties.microclimate_challenge: Extreme radiant heat from metal fabrication & dark slag yards
properties.recommended_action: Dense 30m multi-canopy green shelterbelt to intercept convective heat plumes
properties.projected_cooling_potential: -5.8 °C cooling deficit vs canopy reference (upper bound, not a measured effect)

properties.site_name: Site #2: Jagadamba Commercial Core & Transit Nexus
properties.microclimate_challenge: High pedestrian density, unshaded asphalt canyon, heavy concrete thermal mass
properties.recommended_action: Continuous shaded street tree canopy, pocket bioswales, and green transit shelters
properties.projected_cooling_potential: -5.2 °C cooling deficit vs canopy reference (upper bound, not a measured effect)

properties.site_name: Site #3: Outer Harbour Logistics & Freight Yard
properties.microclimate_challenge: Unvegetated storage yards, high maritime humidity coupled with heat traps
